literature.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 诺如病毒 GII.4 的总体感染率为每 1000 人年 205 例感染(后中位数;95% 可信区间:191-210),跨年范围为每 1000 人年 36-486 例感染(后中位数范围)。 [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014059]
英国卫生安全局的报告显示,过去两周,英格兰的 诺如病毒 病例增加了 35% 以上,总病例数比典型季节性水平高出约 5%。苏格兰的病例有所下降,但威尔士的病例有所增加。 [10.64628/ab.tkxj43hyq]
在 1353 名成人和 93 名儿童中,63% 的成人和 61% 的儿童返回了血液样本。其中,88% 被认为可以进行处理,100% 的可行样本具有足够的体积和质量,可以进行 诺如病毒 抗体的处理和评估。 [10.7812/tpp/26.133]
在猫、狗、几种鸭类和鸡的血清中观察到针对多种抗原的高抗体滴度,而在大鼠、猪、马和野猪的血清中观察到滴度较低、基因型较少的抗体。来自猕猴、海狮、港湾鼠海豚、牛、绵羊、山羊和血清素蝙蝠的血清显示出低或不可检测的抗体滴度。九十五个样本表现出免疫显性反应,定义为一到三个基因型表现出比其余基因型的几何平均值更高的抗体滴度。 [10.1128/spectrum.02716-26]
主要气候调整 ARMA(2,0) 模型显示,2020 年 2 月 OID 报告减少了 48.1%,随后每月增加 2.15%。斜率变化为每月 1.13%,置信区间为零。2022 年 1 月的敏感性模型估计,突破后的正趋势为每月 3.28%,但其斜率变化也包括零。 [10.1038/s41598-026-74634-w]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Overall infection rates with norovirus GII.4 were 205 infections per 1000 person-years (posterior median; 95% credible intervals: 191–210) with a range across years of 36–486 infections per 1000 person-years (range of posterior medians). [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014059]

Reports from the UK Health Security Agency indicate that norovirus cases in England have increased by more than 35% over the past two weeks, with overall case numbers about 5% above typical seasonal levels. Cases have fallen in Scotland but risen in Wales. [10.64628/ab.tkxj43hyq]

Of the 1353 adults and 93 children, 63% of adults and 61% of children returned a blood specimen. Of these, 88% were deemed viable for processing, and 100% of viable specimens were of sufficient volume and quality to be processed and assessed for norovirus antibodies. [10.7812/tpp/26.133]

High antibody titers to multiple antigens were observed in sera from cats, dogs, and several duck species, and chickens, whereas lower titers to fewer genotypes were observed in sera from rats, pigs, horses, and wild boar. [10.1128/spectrum.02716-26]

The primary climate-adjusted ARMA(2,0) model showed a 48.1% decrease in OID reports at February 2020, followed by a 2.15% monthly increase. The slope change was 1.13% per month, with a confidence interval spanning zero. [10.1038/s41598-026-74634-w]

news.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 对 2,161 篇有关儿科 诺如病毒 感染的出版物进行了全面的文献计量分析,揭示了研究成果和合作网络的趋势。Bioengineer.org 将这项研究作为科学评论进行了报道。 [news-09585b6a40e6a127]
一项数学建模研究评估了英格兰儿童急性胃肠炎的诺如病毒 GII.4 血清学样本,揭示了高感染率和免疫印迹效应。该研究结果由Bioengineer.org于2026年11月23日报道。 [news-68e4e03776a7832a]
一项广泛的分子 监测 研究在中国 200 个灌溉用水点样本中的 17 个中检测到了 监测 污染,与春季相比,冬季的检测率出现了明显的峰值。该研究于2026年11月21日由Bioengineer.org报道,并根据分子监测的结果得到证实。 [news-588affa387e0e70a]
据 WBTV 报道,北卡罗来纳州一所小学的 100 多名学生和教职员工出现胃肠道症状。 [news-8cf5a51cd3b49679]
诺如病毒旗下一艘游轮暴发造成148名乘客和船员患病。CDC 确认 134 名乘客和 14 名机组人员出现符合 诺如病毒 的症状。暴发 于 2026 年 11 月 15 日向 CDC 报告,但其原因仍不清楚。 [news-30eec71663be6bb4]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Norovirus news developments.
key_findings_en: A comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 2,161 publications on pediatric norovirus infections was conducted, revealing trends in research output and collaboration networks. The study is reported by Bioengineer.org as a scientific review. [news-09585b6a40e6a127]

A mathematical modeling study evaluated pediatric norovirus GII.4 serology samples in England, revealing high infection rates and immune imprinting effects. The findings were reported by Bioengineer.org on November 23, 2026. [news-68e4e03776a7832a]

An extensive molecular surveillance study detected norovirus contamination in seventeen of two hundred sampled irrigation water sites across China, showing a marked winter peak in detection rates compared to spring. [news-588affa387e0e70a]
A norovirus outbreak caused gastrointestinal symptoms in over 100 students and staff at a North Carolina elementary school, as reported by WBTV. [news-8cf5a51cd3b49679]

A cruise ship outbreak of norovirus sickened 148 passengers and crew members. The CDC confirmed symptoms consistent with norovirus in 134 passengers and 14 crew members. The outbreak was reported to the CDC on November 15, 2026, but its cause remains unknown. [news-30eec71663be6bb4]

A comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 2,161 publications on pediatric norovirus infections was conducted, revealing trends in research output and collaboration networks.
A mathematical modeling study evaluated pediatric norovirus GII.4 serology samples in England, revealing high infection rates and immune imprinting effects.

papers.title: Estimation of annual exposures and antibody kinetics against norovirus GII.4 variants from English serology data, 2007–2012
papers.abstract: Norovirus in humans is highly contagious, causing diarrhoea and vomiting, and is especially common in young children. Winter incidence varies annually, and previous research indicates that the change of dominant norovirus variant is followed by high incidence, but having a clear mechanism to explain this observation could support better prediction of epidemics. Here we analyse unique norovirus GII.4 serology blockade data from 656 children in England collected via opportunistic sampling between 2007–2012 using a mathematical model of multi-variant antibody kinetics to infer metrics such as annual attack rates and age-specific infection rates. Analysis reveals that overall infection rates with norovirus GII.4 were 205 infections per 1000 person-years (posterior median; 95% credible intervals: 191–210) with a range across years of 36–486 infections per 1000 person-years (range of posterior medians). Infection rates were lowest in children aged under 1 year at 161 infections per 1000 person-years (95% CrI: 121–210) and highest in children aged 5 years and older, at 250 infections per 1000 person-years (95% CrI: 213–289). The annual attack rate was highest in 2002, coincident with transition of the dominant variant to Farmington Hills, and frequently observed with emergence of new variants, but not always. Parameter estimates indicate moderate evidence for the immune imprinting hypothesis: a stronger antibody response to variants encountered earliest in life. Infection rates estimated here are higher than incidence reported within similar settings based on disease only and is consistent with considerable asymptomatic infection. The combined use of multi-variant antibody data and a mathematical model provide key insights on the natural history of norovirus variants which can inform epidemic planning.

papers.abstract_zh: 诺如病毒 在人类中具有高度传染性,导致腹泻和呕吐,在幼儿中尤其常见。冬季发病率每年都会发生变化,之前的研究表明,显性发病率变异的变化之后是高发病率,但有一个明确的机制来解释这一观察结果可以支持更好地预测流行病。在这里,我们分析了独特的 诺如病毒 GII.4 血清学 封锁数据,这些数据来自 2007 年至 2012 年期间通过机会性抽样收集的 656 名英格兰儿童,使用多变体抗体动力学数学模型来推断年度发病率和特定年龄感染率等指标。分析显示,诺如病毒 GII.4 的总体感染率为每 1000 人年 205 例感染(后中位数;95% 可信区间:191-210),跨年范围为每 1000 人年 36-486 例感染(后中位数范围)。1 岁以下儿童的感染率最低,每 1000 人年有 161 例感染(95% CrI:121-210),5 岁及以上儿童感染率最高,每 1000 人年有 250 例感染(95% CrI:213-289)。2002 年的年度攻击率最高,与主要变种向法明顿山的转变同时发生,并且经常观察到新变种的出现,但并非总是如此。参数估计表明免疫印记假说有适度的证据:对生命早期遇到的变异有更强的抗体反应。这里估计的感染率高于 发病率 在仅基于疾病的类似环境中报告的感染率,并且与大量无症状感染一致。多变体抗体数据和数学模型的结合使用提供了关于 诺如病毒 变体自然史的重要见解,可以为流行病规划提供信息。

papers.title: Profiling of antibody responses to human norovirus in animals
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Noroviruses are a major cause of acute gastroenteritis globally, with over 30 genotypes circulating in humans, some widespread, and others sporadically detected. Human noroviruses have been detected in a variety of animal species, raising the possibility that animals may serve as reservoirs or intermediate hosts for emerging human norovirus strains. To assess whether serology can reveal the circulation of human norovirus genotypes in animals, we analyzed antibody responses in 465 sera from 17 animal species using a previously established multiplex protein microarray containing P-particle antigens from 30 GI, GII, GIV, and GVI genotypes. High antibody titers to multiple antigens were observed in sera from cats, dogs, and several duck species, and chickens, whereas lower titers to fewer genotypes were observed in sera from rats, pigs, horses, and wild boar. Sera from macaques, sea lions, harbor porpoises, cattle, sheep, goats, and serotine bats showed low or undetectable antibody titers. Although we detected antibodies to common human genotypes in cats and dogs, antibodies in other animal species were primarily directed against sporadically reported genotypes. Ninety-five samples exhibited immunodominant responses, defined as one to three genotypes exhibiting higher antibody titers than the geometric mean of the remaining genotypes, and therefore suggestive of genotype-specific recognition. Binding-blocking assays performed on selected sera confirmed some antibody responses observed on the array. Although we find no clear evidence of human norovirus circulation in animals, the strong and broadly reactive antibody profiles observed in cats, dogs, and birds warrant further investigation. IMPORTANCE Human noroviruses have been detected in multiple animal species, raising concerns that animals could act as reservoirs or intermediate hosts for emerging human norovirus strains. However, it remains unclear whether serological responses in animals reflect true circulation of human noroviruses or instead cross-reactive antibody recognition. Using a multiplex protein microarray spanning 30 norovirus genotypes, we profiled antibody responses in sera from 17 animal species. We detected broad antibody responses in cats, dogs, and several bird species, but found little evidence of consistent norovirus genotype-specific recognition. Binding-blocking assays confirmed some of the detected antibody responses. Together, our findings suggest that most antibody responses in animals likely reflect cross-reactivity or non-specific binding rather than widespread circulation of human noroviruses.
authors: Marco W. G. van de Bildt
Joke W. B. van der Giessen

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate whether serology could reveal the circulation of human norovirus genotypes in animals. Using a multiplex protein microarray, antibody responses were analyzed in sera from 17 animal species. High antibody titers were observed in cats, dogs, and several bird species, while lower titers were found in others. papers.title_zh: 动物体内对人 诺如病毒 的抗体反应分析
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Noroviruses are a major cause of acute gastroenteritis globally, with over 30 genotypes circulating in humans, some widespread, and others sporadically detected. Human noroviruses have been detected in a variety of animal species, raising the possibility that animals may serve as reservoirs or intermediate hosts for emerging human norovirus strains. To assess whether serology can reveal the circulation of human norovirus genotypes in animals, we analyzed antibody responses in 465 sera from 17 animal species using a previously established multiplex protein microarray containing P-particle antigens from 30 GI, GII, GIV, and GVI genotypes. High antibody titers to multiple antigens were observed in sera from cats, dogs, and several duck species, and chickens, whereas lower titers to fewer genotypes were observed in sera from rats, pigs, horses, and wild boar. Sera from macaques, sea lions, harbor porpoises, cattle, sheep, goats, and serotine bats showed low or undetectable antibody titers. Although we detected antibodies to common human genotypes in cats and dogs, antibodies in other animal species were primarily directed against sporadically reported genotypes. Ninety-five samples exhibited immunodominant responses, defined as one to three genotypes exhibiting higher antibody titers than the geometric mean of the remaining genotypes, and therefore suggestive of genotype-specific recognition. Binding-blocking assays performed on selected sera confirmed some antibody responses observed on the array. Although we find no clear evidence of human norovirus circulation in animals, the strong and broadly reactive antibody profiles observed in cats, dogs, and birds warrant further investigation. IMPORTANCE Human noroviruses have been detected in multiple animal species, raising concerns that animals could act as reservoirs or intermediate hosts for emerging human norovirus strains. However, it remains unclear whether serological responses in animals reflect true circulation of human noroviruses or instead cross-reactive antibody recognition. Using a multiplex protein microarray spanning 30 norovirus genotypes, we profiled antibody responses in sera from 17 animal species. We detected broad antibody responses in cats, dogs, and several bird species, but found little evidence of consistent norovirus genotype-specific recognition. Binding-blocking assays confirmed some of the detected antibody responses. Together, our findings suggest that most antibody responses in animals likely reflect cross-reactivity or non-specific binding rather than widespread circulation of human noroviruses.

papers.title: Feasibility and Usability of Self-Collected Blood Samples for Studies of Norovirus and Acute Gastroenteritis
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tasso self-collection blood kits have been validated against venous blood-derived serum samples, but not for studies of acute gastroenteritis (AGE). The authors' objectives were to describe the performance of the Tasso+ for self-collection of blood samples among adults and children enrolled in a study of medically attended AGE and to describe specimen processing and antibody testing success. METHODS: The authors used the Tasso+ device for self-collection of blood samples within a prospective cohort study at Kaiser Permanente Northwest. Serum samples were assessed for the presence of antibodies against the norovirus capsid protein. RESULTS: Of a total of 1353 adults and 93 children, 63% of adults and 61% of children returned a blood specimen. Of these, 88% were deemed viable for processing, and 100% of viable specimens were of sufficient volume and quality to be processed and assessed for norovirus antibodies. CONCLUSIONS: The results suggested that Tasso+ is a feasible blood collection tool for studies of AGE and can contribute to the authors' understanding of immune response after natural infection and potentially help identify correlates of protection against severe norovirus disease.

papers.title: Changing seasonality and trends of other infectious diarrhea and norovirus across the pandemic era in Shenzhen China
papers.abstract: Other infectious diarrhea (OID) is a heterogeneous surveillance syndrome whose temporal patterns may change with transmission, pathogen composition, care seeking and reporting. We analyzed 578,222 OID reports from Shenzhen, China, from 1 January 2013 to 31 July 2025, together with monthly norovirus GI-positive, GII-positive and mixed GI + GII-positive series. Calendar-month distributions differed across pre-COVID-19, during COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 periods for all four series. Autocorrelation-aware breakpoint profiling with adjustment for temperature, relative humidity and wet-day frequency favored February 2020, whereas independent-error profiling favored January 2022. In the primary climate-adjusted ARMA(2,0) model, OID reports fell 48.1% at February 2020, then increased by 2.15% per month. The slope change was 1.13% per month, with a confidence interval spanning zero. A January 2022 sensitivity model estimated a positive post-break trend of 3.28% per month, but its slope change also included zero. A three-segment model found no additional acceleration in January 2022 relative to 2020–2021. Available meteorological covariates did not explain the positive later trend. These findings support changing surveillance dynamics across the COVID-19 era, but not a unique or causal 2022 acceleration.

papers.title: Symmetry-breaking antibody binding reveals extensive capsid malleability in pandemic human norovirus
papers.abstract: Virus capsids are metastable assemblies with an exquisite balance between stability and flexibility, obligatory for entry, infectivity, and immune escape. Yet the extent to which human viruses exploit capsid plasticity and how that consequently shapes antigenic landscapes remains poorly understood. Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are the leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide. GII.4 HuNoVs have been evolving epochally, driving most global pandemics, and since 2012, GII.4 Sydney has been the dominant variant. The major capsid protein, VP1, is central to infectivity and immune recognition, and VP1-based virus-like particles (VLPs) are considered promising vaccine candidates. Yet, how the icosahedral HuNoV capsid responds to antibody pressure at the atomic level remains unclear. Here, we present the first atomic structure of GII.4 Sydney capsid determined by cryo-EM, revealing the structural features that likely contribute to its sustained dominance. Using focused refinement, we uncover the remarkable capsid plasticity in response to symmetry-breaking binding of neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibodies. VP1 adopts 11 distinct conformational modalities to accommodate asymmetric antibody binding, and antibody-disrupted VLPs reassemble into smaller particles with five additional VP1 states. This previously unrecognized extent of conformational adaptability provides key insights for designing next-generation VLP- or mRNA-based vaccines targeting HuNoV infections.

papers.title: Clinical complications during hospitalizations of all-cause and norovirus acute gastroenteritis among adults in the United States, 2022–2024
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Although norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) globally, contemporary data describing the clinical spectrum of hospitalized all-cause and norovirus-associated AGE are limited. We characterized clinical complications during acute hospitalizations among adults with all-cause and norovirus AGE. Methods We conducted a descriptive study using Optum’s de-identified Clinformatics ® Data Mart (Optum® CDM) administrative claims database. Adults aged ≥ 18 years with hospitalized all-cause AGE or norovirus-specified episodes between July 2022 and June 2024 were identified using ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes. Clinical complications during acute hospitalizations occurring within 3 days of the index episode were evaluated by age group (18–59 and ≥ 60 years) and presence of underlying medical conditions. Baseline frailty among adults aged ≥ 60 years was assessed using a validated claims-based frailty index. Results The study included 192,430 hospitalized all-cause AGE episodes and 2,589 hospitalized norovirus-coded episodes. Patients were predominantly older adults (median age, 74 years) with multiple underlying medical conditions. Metabolic disturbances, acute kidney injury, dehydration, and sepsis were the most common complications among patients with all-cause AGE (57.2%, 38.3%, 29.2%, and 26.5%, respectively) or norovirus-coded episodes (62.0%, 42.6%, 41.9%, and 28.1%, respectively). High frequencies of complications were also observed among younger adults with norovirus hospitalizations. Among adults aged ≥ 60 years, baseline frailty was substantially higher among patients with underlying medical conditions than among those without. Conclusions Hospitalized adults with all-cause and norovirus-coded AGE commonly experienced renal, metabolic, and systemic complications. Older adults demonstrated substantial baseline frailty, while severe complications also occurred among younger adults hospitalized with norovirus illness. These findings improve the clinical characterization of severe AGE, specifically norovirus, and identify populations at greatest risk for adverse outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize clinical complications during hospitalizations for all-cause and norovirus-associated acute gastroenteritis (AGE) among adults in the United States from 2022 to 2024. Using Optum’s administrative claims database, researchers identified 192,430 all-cause AGE episodes and 2,589 norovirus-coded episodes. They found that metabolic disturbances, acute kidney injury, dehydration, and sepsis were the most common complications, with high frequencies observed in both older and younger adults. The study highlights the need for improved clinical management and prevention strategies for severe AGE, particularly among adults with norovirus infection. However, the reliance on administrative data introduces potential biases, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 诺如病毒 是全球 急性胃肠炎 (AGE) 的主要原因,但有关全因住院期间临床并发症和 诺如病毒 相关 AGE 的当代数据有限。本研究旨在描述全因年龄和 诺如病毒 年龄成人急性住院期间的临床并发症特征。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 Optum 的去识别化 Clinformatics® Data Mart (Optum® CDM) 管理索赔数据库进行了一项描述性研究。使用 ICD-10-CM 诊断 代码识别 2022 年 7 月至 2024 年 6 月期间因全因 AGE 或 诺如病毒 特定事件住院的 18 岁以上成年人。
elements_zh.methods: 使用经过验证的基于索赔的虚弱指数评估 60 岁以上成年人的基线虚弱程度。按年龄组(18-59 岁和 ≥ 60 岁)和是否存在基础医疗状况对首发 3 天内发生的急性住院期间的临床并发症进行评估。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究包括 192,430 例住院的全因 AGE 发作和 2,589 例住院的 诺如病毒 编码发作。代谢紊乱、急性肾损伤、脱水和脓毒症是全因 AGE(分别为 57.2%、38.3%、29.2% 和 26.5%)或 诺如病毒 编码发作(分别为 62.0%、42.6%、41.9% 和 28.1%)患者中最常见的并发症。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,患有全因和 诺如病毒 编码 AGE 的住院成人通常会出现肾脏、代谢和全身并发症。这些发现改善了严重 AGE(特别是 诺如病毒)的临床特征,并确定了不良结果风险最大的人群。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为有针对性的 监测 和严重 AGE 的风险评估提供信息,特别是在 诺如病毒 感染的成年人中,并强调需要改进高危人群的临床管理和预防策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖行政索赔数据而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差并缺乏详细的临床信息。证据是中等的,因为它提供了对并发症的描述性见解,但没有建立因果关系。

papers.full_text: Described as the “Ferrari of the virus world” for the way it races from person to person, norovirus is once again on the move as we head into winter. Reports from the UK Health Security Agency have highlighted that cases of norovirus – commonly known as the “winter vomiting bug” – have increased by more than 35% in England over the past two weeks, compared with the previous fortnight. While that sounds alarming, this is still within expected levels for the season. Overall case numbers are about 5% above what’s typical for this time of year. Cases have fallen in Scotland, but Wales has seen a rise. Norovirus symptoms include sudden-onset nausea, diarrhoea and vomiting, sometimes accompanied by fever, stomach pain, body aches and headaches. Most healthy adults recover within one to three days. However, those with weakened immune systems, older adults and young children face a higher risk of severe symptoms. When this happens, people can be ill for much longer and may need hospital treatment if they become dehydrated. Norovirus is highly contagious, with some studies suggesting that as few as ten virus particles can cause an infection. It spreads from person to person when tiny amounts of virus from infected faeces or vomit get on to food, hands or surfaces and are then transferred to the mouth. Close contact between people can also spread the virus. This may help explain why cases peak in winter, when people spend more time together indoors. However, you can catch it at any time of the year. The virus is also particularly resilient; it can survive on hard kitchen surfaces such as stainless steel and ceramic for up to two weeks, and it takes temperatures of around 60°C to kill it. There are no approved vaccines or specific treatments for norovirus. It evolves quickly to escape our immune systems, and has proved notoriously difficult to grow in the lab, which has hampered research efforts. That said, recent breakthroughs in growing norovirus using lab-grown human gut cells may make it easier to develop treatments in future. How to protect yourself and your household While alcohol-based hand sanitisers can be effective against other viruses, such as the ones that cause COVID and flu, they don’t work well against norovirus. Instead, the best way to protect yourself is by washing your hands often with soap and hot water, ideally for 15 seconds or more. This is particularly important before or after preparing food, and after going to the toilet. Norovirus is also frequently spread through contaminated food. Fresh produce such as fruit and vegetables may pick up the virus during harvesting, packaging or handling, so wash these thoroughly before use. Shellfish such as oysters can also be contaminated with concentrated norovirus from the water they live in, so ensure these are thoroughly cooked, rather than steamed or eaten raw. If someone in your household has norovirus, cleaning surfaces regularly with bleach-based products can help prevent the virus from spreading. Using a dummy called Vomiting Larry, researchers found that norovirus-containing droplets can spread around ten feet (three metres) when someone vomits. So, it’s important to immediately clean areas that have been contaminated by vomit or faeces. Frequent cleaning of heavily used surfaces such as door handles, light switches, taps, toilet seats and flush handles, ideally while wearing disposable gloves, can help reduce the chances of the virus spreading. Washing soiled clothes or bedding separately from other laundry, at a temperature of 60°C or above at the longest cycle time possible, can also help kill the virus on soft surfaces. If you are unlucky enough to get norovirus yourself, the only solution is to allow the virus to run its short, but deeply unpleasant, course. Replacing lost fluids is essential, so drink plenty of water, tea or electrolyte drinks, or use oral rehydration sachets. If you feel able to eat, stick to plain foods that are easy to digest, such as toast, rice, pasta or soup, and avoid fatty or salty foods that may make your symptoms worse. As norovirus is highly contagious, ensure that you stay at home and rest as much as possible. Keep your distance from other people in your household where you can, and avoid preparing food for others while you’re unwell and for at least 48 hours after symptoms stop. Even after full recovery, infectious virus can still be shed in poo for up to two weeks, so continuing to frequently clean bathroom areas can help prevent further transmission. With cases rising as winter sets in, the Ferrari of viruses may be doing the rounds for a while yet. A few simple habits could save you, and others, a very unpleasant few days.

papers.title_original: Norovirus is spreading – how to recognise the symptoms and what to do

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the spread of norovirus and its associated symptoms, highlighting the need for awareness and understanding of its seasonal patterns and public health impact. The background emphasized the virus's rapid transmission and its designation as the "Ferrari of the virus world.".
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed reported cases of norovirus in England, Scotland, and Wales over the past two weeks, comparing them to typical seasonal levels. It noted that case numbers in England have increased by more than 35% compared to the previous fortnight, while Scotland has seen a decline and Wales an increase.
analysis.methods: The study relied on data from the UK Health Security Agency, tracking reported cases of norovirus across different regions. It also discussed the virus's transmission mechanisms, including its ability to spread through contaminated surfaces and close contact, and its resilience to heat.
analysis.main_results: Reports from the UK Health Security Agency indicate that norovirus cases in England have increased by more than 35% over the past two weeks, with overall case numbers about 5% above typical seasonal levels. Cases have fallen in Scotland but risen in Wales.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the rise in cases as consistent with seasonal expectations, suggesting that the increase in England may be due to factors like increased indoor contact during winter. They noted that the virus's resilience and rapid evolution pose challenges for research and control efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform public health strategies for norovirus surveillance and prevention, particularly in settings where close contact is common. They also highlight the need for continued research into developing treatments and vaccines due to the virus's rapid evolution and lab-growth difficulties.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on reported case data, which may not capture all instances of norovirus infection. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on observational data rather than controlled experiments.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the recent spread of norovirus in England, Scotland, and Wales, noting a 35% increase in cases over the past two weeks compared to the previous fortnight. While overall case numbers are slightly above seasonal norms, Scotland has seen a decline, and Wales an increase. The paper highlights norovirus's rapid transmission, symptoms, and the challenges in developing treatments due to its quick evolution and difficulty in lab cultivation. It also discusses the virus's resilience to heat and its spread through contaminated surfaces and close contact. The findings suggest that the rise in cases may be linked to increased indoor interactions during winter, but the evidence is moderate due to reliance on observational data. The study underscores the importance of continued surveillance and research into norovirus, given its public health impact and the lack of approved vaccines or treatments.

Arts + Culture Economy Education Environment + Energy Ethics + Religion Health Politics + Society Science + Tech World Podcasts Local Prostock-studio/Shutterstock.com Norovirus is spreading – how to recognise the symptoms and what to do Published: November 24, 2026 6:37am EST Described as the “Ferrari of the virus world” for the way it races from person to person, norovirus is once again on the move as we head into winter. Reports from the UK Health Security Agency have highlighted that cases of norovirus – commonly known as the “winter vomiting bug” – have increased by more than 35% in England over the past two weeks, compared with the previous fortnight. While that sounds alarming, this is still within expected levels for the season. Overall case numbers are about 5% above what’s typical for this time of year. Cases have fallen in Scotland, but Wales has seen a rise. Norovirus symptoms include sudden-onset nausea, diarrhoea and vomiting, sometimes accompanied by fever, stomach pain, body aches and headaches. Most healthy adults recover within one to three days. However, those with weakened immune systems, older adults and young children face a higher risk of severe symptoms. When this happens, people can be ill for much longer and may need hospital treatment if they become dehydrated. Norovirus is highly contagious, with some studies suggesting that as few as ten virus particles can cause an infection. It spreads from person to person when tiny amounts of virus from infected faeces or vomit get on to food, hands or surfaces and are then transferred to the mouth. Close contact between people can also spread the virus. This may help explain why cases peak in winter, when people spend more time together indoors. However, you can catch it at any time of the year. The virus is also particularly resilient; it can survive on hard kitchen surfaces such as stainless steel and ceramic for up to two weeks, and it takes temperatures of around 60°C to kill it. There are no approved vaccines or specific treatments for norovirus. It evolves quickly to escape our immune systems, and has proved notoriously difficult to grow in the lab, which has hampered research efforts. That said, recent breakthroughs in growing norovirus using lab-grown human gut cells may make it easier to develop treatments in future. How to protect yourself and your household While alcohol-based hand sanitisers can be effective against other viruses, such as the ones that cause COVID and flu, they don’t work well against norovirus. Instead, the best way to protect yourself is by washing your hands often with soap and hot water, ideally for 15 seconds or more. This is particularly important before or after preparing food, and after going to the toilet. Norovirus is also frequently spread through contaminated food. Fresh produce such as fruit and vegetables may pick up the virus during harvesting, packaging or handling, so wash these thoroughly before use. Shellfish such as oysters can also be contaminated with concentrated norovirus from the water they live in, so ensure these are thoroughly cooked, rather than steamed or eaten raw. If someone in your household has norovirus, cleaning surfaces regularly with bleach-based products can help prevent the virus from spreading. Using a dummy called Vomiting Larry, researchers found that norovirus-containing droplets can spread around ten feet (three metres) when someone vomits. So, it’s important to immediately clean areas that have been contaminated by vomit or faeces. Vomiting Larry in action. Frequent cleaning of heavily used surfaces such as door handles, light switches, taps, toilet seats and flush handles, ideally while wearing disposable gloves, can help reduce the chances of the virus spreading. Washing soiled clothes or bedding separately from other laundry, at a temperature of 60°C or above at the longest cycle time possible, can also help kill the virus on soft surfaces. If you are unlucky enough to get norovirus yourself, the only solution is to allow the virus to run its short, but deeply unpleasant, course. Replacing lost fluids is essential, so drink plenty of water, tea or electrolyte drinks, or use oral rehydration sachets. If you feel able to eat, stick to plain foods that are easy to digest, such as toast, rice, pasta or soup, and avoid fatty or salty foods that may make your symptoms worse. As norovirus is highly contagious, ensure that you stay at home and rest as much as possible. Keep your distance from other people in your household where you can, and avoid preparing food for others while you’re unwell and for at least 48 hours after symptoms stop. Even after full recovery, infectious virus can still be shed in poo for up to two weeks, so continuing to frequently clean bathroom areas can help prevent further transmission. With cases rising as winter sets in, the Ferrari of viruses may be doing the rounds for a while yet. A few simple habits could save you, and others, a very unpleasant few days. papers.title: The third study of infectious intestinal disease in the community: microbiological methods
papers.abstract: Infectious intestinal disease (IID) is a significant public health concern, with an estimated 17 million cases occurring annually in the UK. The third study of IID in the community (IID3 study) will provide updated estimates of the incidence and aetiology of IID in the UK. This protocol describes the laboratory methods employed by the IID3 study in primary diagnostic and reference laboratories. Stool specimens were obtained from subjects in the UK with symptoms of IID who were prospectively enrolled through primary care in two cohorts from May 2023 to September 2025. Specimens were tested for 21 pathogens using PCR-based methods in two separate workflows at Liverpool Clinical Laboratories. The first workflow comprised EntericBio DX, Viral Panel 3 and Clostridium difficile assays (Serosep, Crawley, UK); and the second a panel of assays for detection of Clostridium perfringens (cpa), Aeromonas spp ., Cyclospora cayetanensis and diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli based on 3base ® Technology [Genetic Signatures (GS), Newtown, Australia]. Specimens that tested positive for Salmonella spp ., Campylobacter spp ., Yersinia spp ., Vibrio spp ., Shigella spp. and diarrhoeagenic E. coli were referred together with the corresponding bacterial isolate to the Gastrointestinal Bacteria Reference Unit, UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Samples that tested positive for Cryptosporidium spp., Giardia duodenalis and Cyclospora cayetanensis were referred for genotyping to the national Cryptosporidium Reference Unit, Public Health Wales. Norovirus-positive faecal specimens were referred for Sanger sequencing-based genotyping to the Enteric Virus Unit, UKHSA. These methods encompassing modern diagnostic and reference microbiology represent a comprehensive approach to the detection and characterization of pathogens causing IID in the UK population and serve as a reference for future studies.

papers.title: HIRSCHSPRUNG DISEASE: WHEN BOWEL DYSFUNCTION TAKES A SYSTEMIC TURN - A CASE REPORT
papers.abstract: Background: Hirschsprung disease (HD) is a rare congenital disorder of the enteric nervous system, caused by impaired neural crest cell migration during intestinal development. This leads to aganglionosis of the distal bowel, most frequently affecting the rectosigmoid colon. Its most feared complication is the Hirschsprung-associated Enterocolitis (HAEC), the leading cause of mortality and morbidity. Case presentation: A 4-year-old boy, with a history of HD treated two years prior with a Swenson pull-through procedure, presented to the paediatric emergency department with a one-day history of abdominal pain, fetid diarrhoea, and vomiting. No other symptoms were recorded. Physical examination revealed no abnormalities. Oral antiemetics and hydration were administered. During hospitalization, he remained lethargic with progressive abdominal distension, for which intravenous fluids were initiated for maintenance and replacement of ongoing losses. Initial laboratory tests and blood cultures were unremarkable. Gastrointestinal molecular panel was positive for norovirus, with a negative stool culture. Abdominal radiography showed marked dilatation of bowel loops and faecal loading (Figure 1). Within six hours, he deteriorated rapidly with the onset of fever, tachycardia, signs of poor peripheral perfusion, and hypotension. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 先天性巨结肠症(HD)是一种罕见的肠神经系统先天性疾病,由肠道发育过程中神经嵴细胞迁移受损引起。这会导致远端肠神经节缺失,最常影响直肠乙状结肠。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是 病例报告 的研究,描述了一名有 HD 病史的 4 岁男孩,两年前接受了 Swenson 拔出手术治疗。他因一天腹痛、恶臭腹泻和呕吐病史到儿科急诊科就诊。没有记录到其他症状。
elements_zh.methods: 给予口服止吐药和水化。在住院期间,他仍然昏昏欲睡,并伴有进行性腹胀,为此开始静脉输液以维持和补充持续的损失。最初的实验室测试和血培养没有异常。胃肠道分子检测 诺如病毒 呈阳性,粪便培养呈阴性。通过放置鼻胃管进行胃肠减压,引流粪便物质,并进行直肠灌肠,将粪便爆炸性排出。
elements_zh.main_results: 腹部X光检查显示肠袢明显扩张和粪便负荷。实验室重新评估显示严重代谢性酸中毒(pH 和 HCO3 低于可测量范围)、高乳酸血症(9.8 mmol/L)、急性肾损伤(肌酐 0.9 mg/dL;较基线增加 2.25 倍)和炎症标志物升高(C 反应蛋白 27.7 mg/dL 和降钙素原 >100 ng/mL),这些结果与表现为混合性严重 HAEC 一致。低血容量/感染性休克。胃残留逐渐减少,腹胀明显改善。12 天后,患者出院,临床和分析结果稳定,肾功能正常。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: HAEC 是一种并发症,20-40% 的 HD 患者在手术前后都可能发生。在初始阶段,临床表现是非特异性的,可以模仿 急性胃肠炎。然而,患者可能会迅速进展为混合性低血容量/分布性(脓毒性)休克。治疗依靠积极的液体治疗来稳定血流动力学和控制胃肠源头。广谱抗生素必须使用七到十天,覆盖厌氧菌和肠道革兰氏阴性菌。胃肠减压至关重要,包括放置鼻胃管、连续直肠冲洗和肠道休息。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 及时的 诊断 和管理需要高度的临床怀疑。研究结果强调了认识到 HAEC 作为 HD 患者潜在并发症的重要性,即使在手术干预后也是如此,并强调需要采取迅速和积极的 治疗 策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性。该证据基于单个 病例报告,其通用性有限。然而,研究结果与 HAEC 和 诺如病毒 感染的已知临床表现一致,支持适度的置信度评估。

papers.title: Eculizumab Therapy in Suspected Late-Onset Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome in an Adult Kidney Transplant Recipient: A Case Report
papers.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a rare, life-threatening, complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) that may occur de novo after kidney transplantation. Because its manifestations overlap with more common causes of allograft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection, diagnosis can be challenging. The disease may progress rapidly, making early clinical suspicion and timely etiologic evaluation essential. Case Presentation: We report a 52-year-old man who developed abrupt, severe graft dysfunction approximately 10 years after ABO-incompatible living-donor kidney transplantation. His serum creatinine had remained approximately 2.0 mg/dL after treatment for suspected chronic active antibody-mediated rejection but increased to 6.57 mg/dL at outpatient follow-up and to 8.47 mg/dL on admission after a recent norovirus infection. Initial evaluation considered common post-transplant causes of graft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection-related injury. However, as renal dysfunction progressed and concurrent anemia and thrombocytopenia became evident, TMA was suspected, and a targeted workup was undertaken. Elevated lactate dehydrogenase, decreased haptoglobin, fragmented red blood cells, and allograft biopsy findings supported TMA. No HLA class I or II antibodies were detected, C4d staining was negative, ADAMTS13 activity was preserved, and testing for Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli was negative. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous CFH variant (c.3329G>C, p.Gly1110Ala), classified as a variant of uncertain significance. Based on the clinical, hematologic, and histopathologic findings, suspected aHUS was considered the most likely diagnosis. However, ABMR-associated TMA could not be completely excluded. Plasma exchange was complicated by anaphylaxis, and eculizumab was initiated. Hematologic abnormalities subsequently resolved, although renal function did not recover and the patient remained dialysis-dependent. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of considering TMA when graft dysfunction progresses rapidly or remains unexplained, even many years after kidney transplantation. Early recognition of microangiopathic features and prompt evaluation for the underlying etiology are particularly important when complement-mediated aHUS is suspected, because established acute-on-chronic allograft injury may limit renal recovery despite hematologic response to C5 inhibition.

papers.title_zh: 依库丽单抗治疗成年肾移植受者疑似晚发型非典型溶血性尿毒症综合征:病例报告
papers.source_body_en: Background and Clinical Significance: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a rare, life-threatening, complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) that may occur de novo after kidney transplantation. Because its manifestations overlap with more common causes of allograft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection, diagnosis can be challenging. The disease may progress rapidly, making early clinical suspicion and timely etiologic evaluation essential. Case Presentation: We report a 52-year-old man who developed abrupt, severe graft dysfunction approximately 10 years after ABO-incompatible living-donor kidney transplantation. His serum creatinine had remained approximately 2.0 mg/dL after treatment for suspected chronic active antibody-mediated rejection but increased to 6.57 mg/dL at outpatient follow-up and to 8.47 mg/dL on admission after a recent norovirus infection. Initial evaluation considered common post-transplant causes of graft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection-related injury. However, as renal dysfunction progressed and concurrent anemia and thrombocytopenia became evident, TMA was suspected, and a targeted workup was undertaken. Elevated lactate dehydrogenase, decreased haptoglobin, fragmented red blood cells, and allograft biopsy findings supported TMA. No HLA class I or II antibodies were detected, C4d staining was negative, ADAMTS13 activity was preserved, and testing for Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli was negative. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous CFH variant (c.3329G>C, p.Gly1110Ala), classified as a variant of uncertain significance. Based on the clinical, hematologic, and histopathologic findings, suspected aHUS was considered the most likely diagnosis. However, ABMR-associated TMA could not be completely excluded. Plasma exchange was complicated by anaphylaxis, and eculizumab was initiated. Hematologic abnormalities subsequently resolved, although renal function did not recover and the patient remained dialysis-dependent. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of considering TMA when graft dysfunction progresses rapidly or remains unexplained, even many years after kidney transplantation. Early recognition of microangiopathic features and prompt evaluation for the underlying etiology are particularly important when complement-mediated aHUS is suspected, because established acute-on-chronic allograft injury may limit renal recovery despite hematologic response to C5 inhibition.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景和临床意义:非典型溶血性尿毒症综合征(aHUS)是一种罕见的、危及生命的、补体介导的血栓性微血管病(TMA),可能在肾移植后重新发生。由于其表现与同种异体移植功能障碍的更常见原因重叠,包括排斥、钙调神经磷酸酶抑制剂毒性和感染,诊断 可能具有挑战性。该疾病可能进展迅速,因此早期临床怀疑和及时的病因学评估至关重要。病例介绍:我们报告一名 52 岁男性,在 ABO 血型不合的活体供体肾移植后约 10 年后突然出现严重的移植物功能障碍。由于疑似慢性活动性抗体介导的排斥反应,在 治疗 治疗后,他的血清肌酐仍保持在约 2.0 mg/dL,但在门诊随访时增加至 6.57 mg/dL,在最近的 诺如病毒 感染后入院时增加至 8.47 mg/dL。初步评估考虑了移植物功能障碍的常见移植后原因,包括排斥、钙调神经磷酸酶抑制剂毒性和感染相关损伤。然而,随着肾功能障碍的进展以及并发贫血和血小板减少症变得明显,怀疑是TMA,并进行了有针对性的检查。乳酸脱氢酶升高、触珠蛋白降低、红细胞碎片和同种异体移植物活检结果支持 TMA。未检测到 HLA I 类或 II 类抗体,C4d 染色呈阴性,ADAMTS13 活性得以保留,产志贺毒素大肠杆菌检测呈阴性。基因检测发现了杂合 CFH 变异(c.3329G>C,p.Gly1110Ala),被归类为意义不确定的变异。根据临床、血液学和组织病理学结果,怀疑 aHUS 被认为是最有可能的 诊断。然而,不能完全排除 ABMR 相关的 TMA。过敏反应使血浆置换变得复杂,因此开始使用依库丽单抗。尽管肾功能没有恢复并且患者仍然依赖透析,但血液学异常随后得到解决。结论:该病例凸显了当移植物功能障碍迅速进展或仍无法解释时(甚至在肾移植后多年)考虑 TMA 的重要性。当怀疑补体介导的 aHUS 时,早期识别微血管病变特征并及时评估潜在病因尤其重要,因为尽管对 C5 抑制有血液学反应,但已确定的慢性同种异体移植物急性损伤可能会限制肾脏恢复。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, November 25, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Norovirus Found in Agricultural Irrigation Water Across China Shows Marked Winter Peak by November 21, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Norovirus Found in Agricultural Irrigation Water Across China Shows Marked Winter Peak Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram An extensive molecular surveillance study examining agricultural irrigation water across twenty-seven cities in China detected norovirus contamination in seventeen of two hundred sampled sites, demonstrating a marked seasonal increase in detection rates during winter compared to spring. The investigation, designed to assess the environmental presence of the virus at an essential interface of food production, employed tangential flow filtration and reverse transcription quantitative real-time PCR to detect viral genomes. Norovirus represents a major etiology of acute gastroenteritis across the globe, and agricultural water supplies have been identified as potential vectors capable of transferring enteric pathogens onto crop surfaces. By tracking both genogroup I and genogroup II lineages across a broad geographical distribution, the researchers aimed to clarify how irrigation sources serve as potential environmental reservoirs and evaluate the direct implications for agricultural produce safety. The structural characteristics and environmental resilience of norovirus contribute significantly to its capacity to persist within agricultural and aquatic systems. The viral capsid protein, designated viral protein 1, mediates host cell recognition and facilitates immune evasion while driving ongoing genetic diversification. Analysis of the gene encoding viral protein 1 categorizes noroviruses into ten distinct genogroups spanning from GI to GX. Within human populations in China, genogroups GI and GII represent the predominant infectious types. Strains belonging to genogroup GI infect humans exclusively, whereas genogroup GII displays a broader host range that encompasses animal reservoirs such as swine, where specific genotypes including GII.11, GII.18, and GII.19 have been identified, pointing to potential cross-species transmission pathways. Understanding transmission routes through agricultural waterways addresses critical aspects of foodborne disease prevention from an integrated One Health perspective. Norovirus exhibits high infectivity, with an infectious dose of fewer than twenty viral particles capable of inducing clinical gastrointestinal illness via the fecal-oral route. Global surveillance indicates that norovirus infections result in hundreds of millions of illnesses annually, accompanied by substantial mortality among vulnerable demographics including infants, elderly individuals, and immunocompromised patients. Because agricultural crops such as lettuce, strawberries, and tomatoes are frequently consumed fresh with minimal processing, contamination during the cultivation phase represents an acute vulnerability. Fecal contamination originating from domestic wastewater, livestock operations, or polluted surface runoff introduces viral particles into irrigation networks, where pathogens can adhere to plant surfaces or become internalized within vegetable tissues, potentially circumventing conventional post-harvest washing procedures. Discover more Soothe Digestion Check Symptoms Study Biology Source Farm Gear water To capture geographical diversity, the research team collected two hundred irrigation water samples between December 2023 and April 2024 across twenty-seven municipalities throughout China. The sampling coverage encompassed a broad variety of agricultural water sources, including rivers, lakes, groundwater systems, and municipal tap water utilized for irrigation purposes. The municipal distribution included one hundred seventeen samples from Beijing, ten from Guilin in Guangxi, seven from Changzhou in Jiangsu, seven from Shijiazhuang in Hebei, six from Chifeng in Nei Mongol, six from Qingdao in Shandong, six from Dali in Yunnan, five from Liuzhou in Guangxi, four from Xinyang in Henan, and three each from Xinxiang, Fuzhou, Changsha, and Zhuzhou. Additional paired samples were obtained from Handan, Jining, Lanzhou, Zhuhai, Changzhi, and Nanning, alongside individual samples from Chaoyang, Luoyang, Dalian, Wuhan, Jilin City, Changchun, Shenyang, and Suzhou. Temporal and spatial classifications were structured to evaluate environmental variation across distinct climatic divisions. Using February 4, 2024, as the chronological boundary, the investigators designated eighteen samples as winter collections and one hundred eighty-two samples as spring collections. Geographically, the sampling points were categorized relative to the Qinling Mountains-Huai River line, which demarcates northern and southern China. Under this division, forty-seven irrigation samples represented southern localities, whereas one hundred fifty-three samples were retrieved from northern regions. This structured division permitted statistical comparisons of viral prevalence across distinct regional hydrology and agricultural management contexts, allowing the authors to examine whether climatic shifts and geographical coordinates correlated with the frequency of detectable viral contamination. Discover more Study Marine Life Order Spring Water Water Methodological quality control was established using murine norovirus strain BJ10-2062 as an operational process control to monitor the efficiency and consistency of viral recovery. Spiking experiments complied with China National Food Safety Standard GB 4789.42-2025, which governs food microbiological examination and norovirus detection, requiring a viral recovery rate exceeding one percent for each evaluated sample batch. Serial ten-fold dilutions ranging from 10^8 down to 10 copies per microliter were quantified to construct a linear standard curve, which yielded a linear regression formula of Y equals minus 3.4705X plus 43.015 with a coefficient of determination of 0.9996, while demonstrating an analytical limit of detection of 100 copies per milliliter. The concentration protocol processed five-hundred-milliliter water volumes spiked with one milliliter of the process control suspension. Samples underwent preliminary vacuum filtration through sequential disc membranes with pore diameters of 0.45 micrometers and 0.22 micrometers to remove coarse particulates. Clarified filtrates were subsequently concentrated through tangential flow filtration utilizing a Viva Flow 50R system operated across a ninety-minute circulation cycle. Retained virions were eluted through a thirty-minute recirculation using thirty milliliters of a three-percent triethylene glycol monobutyl ether buffer containing beef extract powder, Tris, and glycine. Viral precipitation was achieved by adding a concentrated polyethylene glycol eight-thousand and sodium chloride solution, followed by overnight incubation and chilled centrifugation at ten thousand revolutions per minute for fifty minutes at four degrees Celsius. Ribonucleic acid was extracted from the resulting pellet using one milliliter of Trizol reagent prior to complementary DNA synthesis. Across the two hundred tested irrigation water specimens, seventeen samples tested positive for norovirus genomes, establishing an overall detection rate of 8.50 percent. When categorized by specific viral genogroups, genogroup GI was identified in eight samples, representing an individual positivity rate of 4.00 percent, whereas genogroup GII was confirmed in fourteen samples, yielding a positivity rate of 7.00 percent. A subset of five samples, accounting for 2.50 percent of the entire sample cohort, contained detectable genetic material from both GI and GII genogroups simultaneously. Cycle threshold values for confirmed positive reactions spanned from 35.05 to 39.25 for GI targets, and from 33.55 to 39.95 for GII targets. Statistical evaluation revealed a highly significant seasonal disparity in viral contamination between sampling periods. The detection rate of norovirus in agricultural irrigation water during the winter period was significantly elevated compared to the spring sampling period, with chi-square testing yielding a p-value of less than 0.001. In contrast, while the absolute positivity rate among southern samples exceeded that observed in northern samples, the geographic disparity did not achieve statistical significance, returning a p-value of 0.134. The elevated frequency of genogroup GII over genogroup GI observed in the water samples matches epidemiological patterns recorded across clinical gastroenteritis surveillance in China since 2009. Furthermore, the pronounced winter peak aligns with recorded human clinical outbreak dynamics, which historically cluster in China between November and January, suggesting that seasonal increases in community infections correspond with increased environmental viral loading in surrounding agricultural surface waters. Regional detection patterns exhibited local variations, including notable differences between municipal outbreak records and environmental water positivity. Among the one hundred seventeen irrigation samples collected from Beijing, only a single river water collection obtained from Huairou District tested positive for genogroup GII norovirus, suggesting that direct agricultural irrigation water might not serve as the dominant transmission driver in that municipality despite historically high clinical reporting. Conversely, river water samples collected from Shijiazhuang in Hebei Province demonstrated a high positivity rate of five positive samples out of seven tested, aligning with prior local pediatric diarrheal surveys reporting elevated positivity. These findings underline the necessity of sustained, integrated One Health surveillance across environmental, agricultural, and clinical domains to trace norovirus contamination dynamics and safeguard fresh produce supply chains. The investigation, designed to assess the environmental presence of the virus at an essential interface of food production, employed tangential flow filtration and reverse transcription quantitative real-time PCR to detect viral genomes. Norovirus represents a major etiology of acute gastroenteritis across the globe, and agricultural water supplies have been identified as potential vectors capable of transferring enteric pathogens onto crop surfaces. By tracking both genogroup I and genogroup II lineages across a broad geographical distribution, the researchers aimed to clarify how irrigation sources serve as potential environmental reservoirs and evaluate the direct implications for agricultural produce safety. The structural characteristics and environmental resilience of norovirus contribute significantly to its capacity to persist within agricultural and aquatic systems. The viral capsid protein, designated viral protein 1, mediates host cell recognition and facilitates immune evasion while driving ongoing genetic diversification. Analysis of the gene encoding viral protein 1 categorizes noroviruses into ten distinct genogroups spanning from GI to GX. Within human populations in China, genogroups GI and GII represent the predominant infectious types. Strains belonging to genogroup GI infect humans exclusively, whereas genogroup GII displays a broader host range that encompasses animal reservoirs such as swine, where specific genotypes including GII.11, GII.18, and GII.19 have been identified, pointing to potential cross-species transmission pathways. Understanding transmission routes through agricultural waterways addresses critical aspects of foodborne disease prevention from an integrated One Health perspective. Norovirus exhibits high infectivity, with an infectious dose of fewer than twenty viral particles capable of inducing clinical gastrointestinal illness via the fecal-oral route. Global surveillance indicates that norovirus infections result in hundreds of millions of illnesses annually, accompanied by substantial mortality among vulnerable demographics including infants, elderly individuals, and immunocompromised patients. Because agricultural crops such as lettuce, strawberries, and tomatoes are frequently consumed fresh with minimal processing, contamination during the cultivation phase represents an acute vulnerability. Fecal contamination originating from domestic wastewater, livestock operations, or polluted surface runoff introduces viral particles into irrigation networks, where pathogens can adhere to plant surfaces or become internalized within vegetable tissues, potentially circumventing conventional post-harvest washing procedures. Discover more Soothe Digestion Check Symptoms Study Biology Source Farm Gear water To capture geographical diversity, the research team collected two hundred irrigation water samples between December 2023 and April 2024 across twenty-seven municipalities throughout China. The sampling coverage encompassed a broad variety of agricultural water sources, including rivers, lakes, groundwater systems, and municipal tap water utilized for irrigation purposes. The municipal distribution included one hundred seventeen samples from Beijing, ten from Guilin in Guangxi, seven from Changzhou in Jiangsu, seven from Shijiazhuang in Hebei, six from Chifeng in Nei Mongol, six from Qingdao in Shandong, six from Dali in Yunnan, five from Liuzhou in Guangxi, four from Xinyang in Henan, and three each from Xinxiang, Fuzhou, Changsha, and Zhuzhou. Additional paired samples were obtained from Handan, Jining, Lanzhou, Zhuhai, Changzhi, and Nanning, alongside individual samples from Chaoyang, Luoyang, Dalian, Wuhan, Jilin City, Changchun, Shenyang, and Suzhou. Temporal and spatial classifications were structured to evaluate environmental variation across distinct climatic divisions. Using February 4, 2024, as the chronological boundary, the investigators designated eighteen samples as winter collections and one hundred eighty-two samples as spring collections. Geographically, the sampling points were categorized relative to the Qinling Mountains-Huai River line, which demarcates northern and southern China. Under this division, forty-seven irrigation samples represented southern localities, whereas one hundred fifty-three samples were retrieved from northern regions. This structured division permitted statistical comparisons of viral prevalence across distinct regional hydrology and agricultural management contexts, allowing the authors to examine whether climatic shifts and geographical coordinates correlated with the frequency of detectable viral contamination. Discover more Study Marine Life Order Spring Water Water Methodological quality control was established using murine norovirus strain BJ10-2062 as an operational process control to monitor the efficiency and consistency of viral recovery. Spiking experiments complied with China National Food Safety Standard GB 4789.42-2025, which governs food microbiological examination and norovirus detection, requiring a viral recovery rate exceeding one percent for each evaluated sample batch. Serial ten-fold dilutions ranging from 10^8 down to 10 copies per microliter were quantified to construct a linear standard curve, which yielded a linear regression formula of Y equals minus 3.4705X plus 43.015 with a coefficient of determination of 0.9996, while demonstrating an analytical limit of detection of 100 copies per milliliter. The concentration protocol processed five-hundred-milliliter water volumes spiked with one milliliter of the process control suspension. Samples underwent preliminary vacuum filtration through sequential disc membranes with pore diameters of 0.45 micrometers and 0.22 micrometers to remove coarse particulates. Clarified filtrates were subsequently concentrated through tangential flow filtration utilizing a Viva Flow 50R system operated across a ninety-minute circulation cycle. Retained virions were eluted through a thirty-minute recirculation using thirty milliliters of a three-percent triethylene glycol monobutyl ether buffer containing beef extract powder, Tris, and glycine. Viral precipitation was achieved by adding a concentrated polyethylene glycol eight-thousand and sodium chloride solution, followed by overnight incubation and chilled centrifugation at ten thousand revolutions per minute for fifty minutes at four degrees Celsius. Ribonucleic acid was extracted from the resulting pellet using one milliliter of Trizol reagent prior to complementary DNA synthesis. Across the two hundred tested irrigation water specimens, seventeen samples tested positive for norovirus genomes, establishing an overall detection rate of 8.50 percent. When categorized by specific viral genogroups, genogroup GI was identified in eight samples, representing an individual positivity rate of 4.00 percent, whereas genogroup GII was confirmed in fourteen samples, yielding a positivity rate of 7.00 percent. A subset of five samples, accounting for 2.50 percent of the entire sample cohort, contained detectable genetic material from both GI and GII genogroups simultaneously. Cycle threshold values for confirmed positive reactions spanned from 35.05 to 39.25 for GI targets, and from 33.55 to 39.95 for GII targets. Statistical evaluation revealed a highly significant seasonal disparity in viral contamination between sampling periods. The detection rate of norovirus in agricultural irrigation water during the winter period was significantly elevated compared to the spring sampling period, with chi-square testing yielding a p-value of less than 0.001. In contrast, while the absolute positivity rate among southern samples exceeded that observed in northern samples, the geographic disparity did not achieve statistical significance, returning a p-value of 0.134. The elevated frequency of genogroup GII over genogroup GI observed in the water samples matches epidemiological patterns recorded across clinical gastroenteritis surveillance in China since 2009. Furthermore, the pronounced winter peak aligns with recorded human clinical outbreak dynamics, which historically cluster in China between November and January, suggesting that seasonal increases in community infections correspond with increased environmental viral loading in surrounding agricultural surface waters. Regional detection patterns exhibited local variations, including notable differences between municipal outbreak records and environmental water positivity. Among the one hundred seventeen irrigation samples collected from Beijing, only a single river water collection obtained from Huairou District tested positive for genogroup GII norovirus, suggesting that direct agricultural irrigation water might not serve as the dominant transmission driver in that municipality despite historically high clinical reporting. Conversely, river water samples collected from Shijiazhuang in Hebei Province demonstrated a high positivity rate of five positive samples out of seven tested, aligning with prior local pediatric diarrheal surveys reporting elevated positivity. These findings underline the necessity of sustained, integrated One Health surveillance across environmental, agricultural, and clinical domains to trace norovirus contamination dynamics and safeguard fresh produce supply chains. analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Norovirus contamination was found in 17% of the sampled sites, with a significant seasonal increase during winter. The study highlights the potential risk of agricultural produce contamination, particularly for crops like lettuce, strawberries, and tomatoes, which are often consumed raw. analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study employed rigorous methods, including tangential flow filtration and reverse transcription quantitative real-time PCR, and used murine norovirus strain BJ10-2062 as a process control. The results were statistically evaluated, and the methodology was compliant with China National Food Safety Standard GB 4789.42-2025. The findings are confirmed and supported by the evidence provided.

The study highlights the risk of agricultural produce contamination, particularly for crops like lettuce, strawberries, and tomatoes, which are often consumed raw. Norovirus is a highly contagious pathogen in humans that causes diarrhoea and vomiting, spreading with particular frequency among young children. Winter incidence fluctuates annually, and earlier scientific investigations demonstrated that shifts in dominant viral variants typically precede elevated disease incidence across affected communities. To establish clearer biological mechanisms capable of refining epidemic forecasts, researchers examined unique norovirus GII.4 serology blockade measurements collected from 656 English children between 2007 and 2012. The underlying blood samples were gathered through opportunistic sampling protocols and evaluated using a specialized mathematical model simulating multi-variant antibody kinetics. This quantitative framework enabled investigators to reconstruct annual attack rates alongside age-stratified infection frequencies across multiple successive viral seasons. Discover more infectious disease Infection infections Model estimates showed wide annual variation throughout the evaluation window, yielding a range of posterior medians spanning from 36 to 486 infections per 1000 person-years. The annual attack rate peaked in 2002, coinciding directly with the epidemiological transition to the dominant Farmington Hills variant. Heightened attack rates appeared frequently alongside emerging norovirus strains, although researchers noted that this pattern did not occur under every single variant transition. Discover more Study Biology Soothe Digestion Check Symptoms infection Age-stratified analyses revealed that estimated transmission dynamics shifted markedly across child developmental stages. Infection rates were lowest among infants under one year of age, measuring 161 infections per 1000 person-years with a 95 percent credible interval of 121 to 210. Conversely, rates peaked among children aged five years and older, reaching 250 infections per 1000 person-years with a 95 percent credible interval of 213 to 289. Model parameters provided moderate evidence supporting the immune imprinting hypothesis, wherein individuals mount stronger antibody responses against the specific variants encountered earliest in life. The modeled infection rates significantly exceeded previous disease-based incidence figures from comparable environments, a discrepancy consistent with extensive asymptomatic infection. The authors concluded that combining multi-variant antibody data with kinetic models illuminates variant natural history to better guide epidemic preparedness.
